JUDGMENT

Wife and child of Thipparaju filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the insurer and owner of the Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP- 21-TC-2145 alleging that on 05.09.2022 at 4.30 a.m., when Thipparaju along with driver transporting rice bags in Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 from Somandepalle, Andhrapradesh towards Tumkur, near Malappanahalli village, Anand-driver of Mahindra Goods vehilce drove the same negligently on the road containing flood, within the limits of Koratagere P.S., made Thipparaju along with Mahindra Goods vehicle to wash away in he flood, driver - Anand escaped from the flood, after two days, body of Thipparaju was found in the bush by the side of Suvarnamukhi river, within the limits of Akkirampura village,
thereby incident taken place resulting in the death of Thipparaju.
2. As on the date of accident deceased Thipparaju being aged about 42 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/- to Rs.30,000/- per month by working as coolie under respondent No.2.
3.

Regarding incident, Koratagere police registered a case in UDR No.59/2022 under Section 174 of Cr.P.C.
4.

In response to the notice, respondent No.1 Insurance company appeared through his Advocate,
filed written statement denying the liability to pay compensation to the petitioners on the ground that the police have registered UDR case under Section 174 of Cr.P.C. regarding the death of Thipparaju, petition filed on 05.07.2023 regarding the alleged incident dated 05.09.2022 is barred by limitation.

In the written statement respondent No.1 denied the allegation regarding age,
occupation and income of the deceased.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 owner of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 appeared through his advocate, but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 27.11.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 04.09.2022 at about 10.00 p.m., on the road at Mallappanahalli village, Koratagere taluk, in view of the negligent use of the Mahindra Scorpio vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 accident taken place resulting in the death of M.Thipparaju S/o.Somappa?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

7. On 28.05.2024, 05.10.2024, 16.12.2024, 20.02.2025 petitioner No.1-M.Arunamma deposed as P.W.1 and produced 9 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.9.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioners and respondent No.1-Insurance company and perused the records.

9. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.22,91,056/- with current and future interest at 6%p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: In the evidence P.W.1-Arunamma stated that on 05.09.2022 at 4.30 a.m., when her husband Thipparaju and Anand-driver of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 are transporting rice bags from Somandepalle, Andhrapradesh towards Tumkur on the road near Malapanahalli village, within the limits of Koratagere P.S., Anand-driver of Mahindra Goods vehicle drove the same negligently in Suvarnamuki river flood road ditch area, made Thipparaju along with Mahindra Goods vehicle to wash away, after two days, body of Thipparaju was traced in a bush by the side of Suvarnamukhi river within the limits of Akkirampura village, thereby incident taken place resulting in the death of Thipparaju.
11.
In the written statement respondent No.1 Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident.
12. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 submitted that she never witnessed the incident.
P.W.1 stated that Somappa is her father-in-law, who is residing at Somandapalli Mandalam.

sentences.text: Ex.P.1 is the copy of UDR pertaining to UDR No.59/2022 submitted by Koratagere police to Taluk Magistrate noting that on 04.09.2022 at 10.00 p.m. Thipparaju along with Anand,
S / o.
Kollappa

left Somandepalle village by loading rice bags in Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 to reach Tumkur, on the way towards Tumkur on 05.09.2022 at 4.30 a.m. near Malapanahalli village, there was flood-Halla,

while passing the halla, vehicle along with Thipparaju washed away, however, Anand driver of the vehicle escaped, after two days body of Thipparaju was traced in a bush situated at Somandepalle village, within the limits of Akkirampura village.
Ex. P.2 is the copy of Mahazar recorded in the place where body of Thipparaju has been traced.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of inquest mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of P.M.Report.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of complaint dated 06.09.2022 submitted by P.W.1-Arunamma to S.H.O., Koratagere
P.S. Ex.P.6 is the copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.220/2022 registered by Koratagere police regarding missing of Thipparaju, on the basis of complaint presented by Arunamma, W/o.Thipparaju.
14. In this case, respondent No.2 owner of the vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.
15. In the file evidence of Anand, driver of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 is not available.

16. In this case, there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by P.W.1-Arunamma regarding reason, mode and consequence of incident (reason for the death of Thipparaju).
17.

Hence, I have concluded that on 05.09.2022 at 4.30 a.m. when Thipparaju and Anand are transporting rice bags from Somandepalle, Andhrapradesh towards Tumkur in Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC- 2145 near Malappanahalli village, within the limits of Koratagere P.S.,
in the flood due to the negligent use of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145,
Thipparaju along with Mahindra Goods vehicle washed away in the flood, Anand escaped, after two days, body of Thipparaju has been traced in a bush situated by the side of Suvarnamukhi river within the limits of Akkirampura village, thereby incident taken place resulting in the death of Thipparaju.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

In the evidence P.W.1 stated that as on the date of incident, Thipparaju being aged about 42 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/- to Rs.30,000/- per month by working as coolie and used to contribute entire income to the family.
19. In the written statement respondent No.1 denied the allegation regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased Tipparaju.

20. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of incident, her husband neither worked as coolie nor earned Rs.25,000/- to Rs.30,000/- p.m.
21.
In the police records, name of the Thipparaju is noted as one of the inmate of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 on 04.09.2022/05.09.2022 along with rice bags.

sentences.text: In the copy of the Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.9, birth year of Thipparaju is noted as 1981.
In the police records, age of the Thipparaju is noted as 42 years.
Aadhar cards shows that petitioners are the wife and child of Tipparaju.
23. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by petitioners regarding their relationship with the deceased Tipparaju.

24. Hence, I have calculated the compensation under the head of loss of dependency, presuming that as on the date of incident deceased Thipparaju being aged about 41 years/42 years, used to earn approximately Rs.15,500/- p.m. by working as coolie, by adding 25% towards future prospects, by deducting 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses, by applying multiplier '14', in the following terms:
Age of the deceased Thipparaju as on - 41 years/42 the date of incident - years

Monthly income of deceased Thipparaju - Rs.15,500/- as on the date of incident Add:
25% towards future prospects - Rs.19,375/- (15,500/- + 3,875/- = 19,375/-) Less:
1/3rd towards personal expenses - Rs.12,917/- of the deceased Thipparaju (19,375/- -
6,458/- = 12,917/-)

Annual income of the deceased - Rs.1,55,004/-
 12,917/- x12  Multiplier Applicable - 14  Loss of dependency 1,55,004/- x 14 - Rs.21,70,056/-
25.

Hence, I award Rs.21,70,056/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.88,000/-
towards loss of consortium to petitioners No.1 and 2 at the rate of Rs.44,000/- each.

26. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners being wife and daughter of deceased Thipparaju are entitle to receive Rs.22,91,056/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. as compensation from the respondents.
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1.
Loss of dependency 21,70,056-00 2. Loss of estate 16,500-00 3. Funeral expenses 16,500-00 4. Loss of Consortium to 88,000-00 petitioners No.1 & 2 at Rs.44,000/each
Total 22,91,056-00 Arunamma.

sentences.text: In the written statement Respondent No.1 Insurance Company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21- TC-2145 as on the date of incident.
Copy of the policy No.61070031220100000198 available in the file confirms that as on the date of incident, Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 had insurance coverage with respondent No.1.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident, respondent No.2 owner of the Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insurer and owner of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC- 2145 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents No.1 and 2 to pay compensation to the petitioners,

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the insurer and owner of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC- 2145 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.22,91,056/-
(Rupees Twenty Two lakhs Ninety one thousand fifty six only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of the Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-21-TC-2145 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount with interest may be released to the petitioner No.1 by crediting the same to her bank account directly.

Entire compensation allotted in favour of minor petitioner No.2 shall be deposited in the name of petitioner No.2 in any bank till she attains the age of 19 years without permitting to create any encumbrances, reserving liberty to withdraw interest periodically once in three months by petitioner No.1.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 2nd day of May, 2025.)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T. Bangalore.
